title: Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken

description: Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken is a beloved dish featuring perfectly crisp chicken coated in an irresistible sweet, spicy, and tangy sauce. Each bite offers a satisfying crunch followed by a burst of complex flavors, making it a truly addictive culinary experience. This iconic Korean comfort food is perfect for gatherings, late-night snacks, or a flavorful family meal.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Pat the chicken pieces very dry with paper towels. Season them evenly with salt, black pepper, and grated ginger. Set aside to marinate for at least 10 minutes.

instructions.title: Mix the Batter
instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, cornstarch (or potato starch), and baking powder. In a separate bowl, beat the egg with cold water. Gradually add the wet mixture to the dry ingredients, stirring until a smooth, pancake-like batter forms. Ensure there are no lumps.

instructions.title: Prepare the Yangnyeom Sauce
instructions.text: In a small saucepan, combine the gochujang, soy sauce, mirin, corn syrup (or honey), brown sugar, minced garlic, grated ginger, rice vinegar, and sesame oil. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally until the sugar dissolves and the sauce slightly thickens, about 5-7 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside.

instructions.title: First Fry the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a large deep pot or Dutch oven to 340°F (170°C). Dip each chicken piece into the batter, ensuring it's fully coated, then carefully lower it into the hot oil. Fry in batches for about 6-7 minutes per batch, until lightly golden and cooked through. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove chicken with a slotted spoon and place on a wire rack to drain.

instructions.title: Second Fry for Extra Crispiness
instructions.text: Increase the oil temperature to 375°F (190°C). Return all the chicken pieces to the hot oil for a second fry. Fry for another 2-3 minutes, or until deep golden brown and extra crispy. This double-frying technique is crucial for authentic Korean fried chicken crispiness. Remove and drain again on a wire rack.

instructions.title: Coat and Serve
instructions.text: While the chicken is still hot, transfer it to a large bowl. Pour the prepared Yangnyeom sauce over the chicken and gently toss until every piece is evenly coated. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and chopped green onions. Serve immediately and enjoy the perfect balance of sweet, spicy, and crispy!

tips: For the crispiest chicken, ensure your oil temperature is accurate and perform the double-frying technique as instructed. The first fry cooks the chicken, and the second fry creates the irresistible crunch.
Potato starch is often preferred over cornstarch in Korean fried chicken for an even lighter and crispier coating. If unavailable, cornstarch works well.
Serve Yangnyeom chicken immediately after coating to enjoy its optimal crispiness and saucy goodness. Leftovers can be stored in the fridge for up to 2 days, though crispiness will diminish.
